% text-styles — weight, slant, and monospace, one at a time and combined.
%
% One concern: does a style change inside a paragraph survive as emphasis, and does
% it stop where the source stops it? The layout path reads style from the font's
% own descriptor and name, so this is the fixture that fails when a font's traits
% are misread — a bold face not recognized as bold, or an italic run that bleeds
% into the words after it.
%
% Each style sits mid-sentence rather than alone on a line, because a run that
% starts at a paragraph's first character and ends at its last cannot show a
% boundary error. The words on either side are the assertion.
%
% \texttt is included because monospace maps to a code span, which is a different
% emission path: everything inside backticks is literal, so a code span cannot
% carry the other two.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{lmodern}
\pagestyle{empty}
\begin{document}

Plain text with \textbf{bold words} inside it.

Plain text with \textit{italic words} inside it.

Plain text with \textbf{\textit{bold italic words}} inside it.

Plain text with \texttt{monospaced words} inside it.

\end{document}
